These monitors have all been self contained and externally mounted, with masses and power requirements exceeding 1 kg and 2 W - low resource, butnot insignificant. Some of these instruments have housed dosimeters, but none have provided measurements within the other spacecraft units. At the moment, there are no low resource radiation monitors available capable of integration within the spacecraft and its units where the sensitive systems are located and capable to provide useful, unparalleled feedback to satellite operations. The benefits include enabled monitoring of the spacecraft health, and providing useful operational diagnostics, and accurate information on the environment. Radiation monitors are the first modules to be discarded during phase A of design due to additional mass and power budget constraints. This disrupts the huge potential of in-orbit data collection, which affects radiation model accuracy and uncertainty a measure, Radiation monitor will allow to manage approach to radiation effects, potentially extending mission lifetimes and opening the door to widespread use of COTS.
